successors.note: Germany renounced the colony by the Treaty of Versailles (28 June 1919); the Union of South Africa dossier dates its own gain 1920.

land.text: German East Africa (to Britain 7 May 1919, the Tanganyika mandate) and the north-western fifth of Kamerun on the Nigerian border (British Cameroons)

successors.note: Ruanda-Urundi and the Kionga Triangle were detached from German East Africa (see the two entries below); the Kigoma district stayed under Belgian occupation until 1921 (belgian-congo dossier).

successors.note: Occupied by Belgian forces from April-June 1916.

capitals.name: Bagamoyo
capitals.note: GEA infobox 'Bagamoyo (1885-1890)'; seat of German East Africa. Coordinates from the gazetteer place list.

capitals.name: Dar es Salaam
capitals.note: GEA infobox 'Dar es Salaam (1890-1916)'; Tabora was a temporary capital in 1916.

capitals.name: Otjimbingwe
capitals.note: UNVERIFIED span. Commissioner Goering 'established his administration at Otjimbingwe' in May (GSWA page, the 1885 paragraph); the Otjimbingwe page says it 'became the seat of the colonial administration, the de facto capital, in the late 1880s' and that 'the civil administration moved' to Windhoek in 1892. Coordinates 22.3575 S, 16.12861 E from that page; the place is not in the gazetteer.

capitals.name: Windhuk (Windhoek)
capitals.note: From 1892 per the Otjimbingwe page ('the civil administration moved there in 1892'); the GSWA infobox names Windhuk with no year and the Windhoek page (founded 18 October 1890 as a fort) names no capital term. To 1915: Botha reached Windhuk on 5 May and the governor surrendered at Khorab on 9 July 1915. Coordinates from the gazetteer.

capitals.name: Aného (Petit Popo)
capitals.note: 'It was the capital of German Togoland from 1885 to 1887' (Aného page, which gives 6.2333 N, 1.6 E).

capitals.name: Zebe (Sebe)
capitals.note: UNVERIFIED end. 'The nearby town of Zebe became the second capital of German Togoland in 1887' and the capital 'was transferred to Lomé in 1897' (Aného page); the pages give no coordinates for Zebe, so the dot is drawn at Aného, a few kilometres away.

capitals.name: Lomé
capitals.note: Lomé 'becoming the capital of Togoland in 1897' (Lomé page); the German Togoland page already calls it 'the capital' for 1895. Coordinates from the gazetteer place list.

capitals.name: Douala (coastal seat of German rule in Kamerun)
capitals.note: UNVERIFIED span. The colonization page calls Douala 'the centre of German rule on the coast'; no page opened names a Kamerun capital before Buea in 1901. Douala fell on 27 September 1914 (Kamerun campaign page). Coordinates from the gazetteer place list.

capitals.name: Buea
capitals.note: 'Buea was the colonial capital of German Kamerun from 1901 to 1919' (Buea page); the span ends in 1914 because the Kamerun campaign page has the Germans retreating to 'the new capital at Jaunde' by 1915. Coordinates from the gazetteer.

capitals.name: Jaunde (Yaoundé)
capitals.note: The Kamerun infobox lists 'Jaunde'; the campaign page calls it the new capital after Douala fell and has the Allies 'pressing in on Jaunde' in early 1916. Coordinates from the gazetteer place list. Span from 1914 is the page's 'new capital'; no page gives the month of the move.

2.67 M km2 against the sum of the infobox areas, 995,000 + 835,100 + 790,000 (Kamerun 1912) + 90,400 = 2.71 M km2: ratio 0.99. The jump from 1910 is Neukamerun (Central African Republic 603 cells, Congo 437, Gabon 293: about 337,000 km2 against the Agadir page's 275,000 km2 for 'Neukamerun'), the 4 November 1911 Franco-German accord. ledger.note: 24 April 1884: Bismarck places Angra Pequena under German protection, the first German colony in Africa. 'On 24 April 1884, he placed the area under the protection of Imperial Germany'; the flag was raised on 7 August 1884. The colonization page calls it 'the first official German colony on African soil'.

region.text: a stretch of territory along the Slave Coast

ledger.note: 5 July 1884: Nachtigal makes Togoland a German protectorate. 'On 5 July 1884 Nachtigal signed a treaty with the local chief, Mlapa III' and 'declared a German protectorate over a stretch of territory along the Slave Coast'. The colonization page puts the Mlapa treaty on 24 April 1884; the Togoland page's date is used.

17 August 1884: the Protectorate of Cameroon begins. 'The official beginning of the German Protectorate of Cameroon was on 17 August 1884'; Nachtigal 'had arrived in Duala in July and negotiated a treaty with a number of rulers local to the region around Duala'.

region.text: South West Africa as Cliopatria draws it in 1885, without the Caprivi Strip

ledger.note: 1885: the German claim covers all of South West Africa. The page dates only the protectorate (24 April 1884) and the 1890 boundary fixing; Cliopatria's 1885 shape has Namibia entire bar the Caprivi Strip, and this event bridges that silence. Walvis Bay remained a British enclave.

minus.text: the Sultan's mainland coastal strip (Cliopatria's 1888 Zanzibar shape cut by the Tanganyika mainland, 71 cells; the pages give no line)

region.text: German East Africa outside the Sultan's 16 km coastal strip

ledger.note: 27 February 1885: Bismarck's charter founds German East Africa under the German East Africa Company. 'signed by Chancellor Otto von Bismarck on 27 February 1885'; announced 3 March; Bismarck's warships 'arrived on 7 August 1885' and the Sultan of Zanzibar accepted German claims outside a 16 km coastal strip. The strip is not drawn German until the 1888 lease (next event): the 1886 Anglo-German agreement respected the Sultan's sovereignty over it (GEA page).

region.text: the Sultan's mainland coastal strip (Cliopatria's 1888 Zanzibar shape cut by the Tanganyika mainland, 71 cells; the pages give no line)

ledger.note: 28 April 1888: the Sultan leases his mainland coast to the German East Africa Company. 'On 28 April 1888, Sultan Khalifah bin Said finally signed a treaty' leasing the coastal strip to the company; 'From August 1888, the company tried to take over the coastal towns', which set off the Abushiri revolt, and the German government 'assumed control of German East Africa' on 1 January 1891. The page calls it a lease, not a cession; the Zanzibar dossier books the same as a loss, and no page opened dates a later purchase.

region.text: Togoland inland, including the Ghana part (later British Togoland)

ledger.note: 1890: Togoland reaches its inland extent. Cliopatria's Togo piece grows from 14 to 275 cells (plus 85 Ghana cells) between 1889 and 1890, about the 90,400 km2 the Togoland page gives (year not stated); the page dates no inland treaty.

region.text: Kamerun inland of the Douala coast

ledger.note: 1890: Kamerun grows inland (Cliopatria 65 to 440 cells). The page is silent on dated treaties or campaigns for 1885-1894.
1890: the seat of German East Africa moves from Bagamoyo to Dar es Salaam. GEA infobox: 'Bagamoyo (1885-1890), Dar es Salaam (1890-1916)'.

July 1890: the Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty gives Germany the Caprivi Strip. 'the colony grew in size through the acquisition of the Caprivi Strip', dated 'In July of the same year'; the GEA page dates the treaty 1 July 1890 and a footnote says 'the boundaries of German South-West Africa were fixed in their present position'.

region.text: the Kionga Triangle south of the Rovuma mouth

ledger.note: 1894: Germany takes the Kionga Triangle from Portugal. The page: Germany 'virtually forced Portugal to cede the triangle in 1894'.

1895: Kamerun grows inland (Cliopatria 440 to 1,297 cells) during Puttkammer's governorship ('1895 to 1906', 'military campaigns against groups such as the Bali'); the page gives no dated treaty or border.

region.text: Ruanda, the north-west of German East Africa

ledger.note: 1898: German control of Rwanda (Cliopatria 9 to 86 of 88 cells). The GEA page says only that Rwanda and Burundi 'were also under the control of German Africa at various points'; no date. Bridging. Review check: the Ruanda-Urundi page (opened 2026-10-25) says 'the German Empire established a presence in Rwanda' in 1897 'with the formation of an alliance with the king' and calls both kingdoms 'two districts of German East Africa' without a date; that fits the 1897 dissolve of kingdom-of-rwanda better than Cliopatria's 1898, so the date stays a bridge (confidence 1).

region.text: Urundi, the north-west of German East Africa

ledger.note: 1900: German control of Burundi (Cliopatria 18 to 91 of 94 cells). The GEA page gives no date for Urundi. Bridging.

region.text: northern and eastern Kamerun (Adamawa, Chad shore) added since 1900

ledger.note: 1905: Kamerun reaches its northern and eastern hinterland (Cliopatria Cameroon 1,297 to 1,949 cells, 493,000 km2, against the infobox's 495,000 km2 for 1910), with slivers of Nigeria and Chad. The page is silent on the campaigns and the 1893-1909 border treaties.

region.text: Neukamerun: the part of Cliopatria's 1911 shape that is not in the 1905 shape

ledger.note: 4 November 1911: Neukamerun. The Franco-German Accord gave Germany a 275,000 km2 territory that became part of German Kamerun, which 'gave Germany an outlet on the Congo River', in return for accepting France's position in Morocco. The page names the land only as territory in French Middle Congo; the region is Cliopatria's 1911 enlargement.

region.text: the small area southeast of Fort Lamy

ledger.note: 4 November 1911: in the same accord Germany ceded 'a small area of territory to the southeast of Fort Lamy' to French Chad.

6 August 1914: the Allies invade Kamerun. 'The first Allied expeditions into the colony on 6 August 1914 were from the east conducted by French troops'; by 25 August British forces from Nigeria had entered from three points; Douala surrendered on 27 September 1914.

7 August 1914: French and British troops invade Togoland. 'After calling on the German colony to surrender on 6 August 1914, French and British troops invaded unopposed the next day.' The British share (Gold Coast forces) is not separated by the page.

7 August 1914: the British share of the Togoland invasion. The page names 'French and British troops'; the British zone is the western part (the Ghana piece of the colony), the French the Togo piece, a split that is the researcher's reading of the 27 December 1916 zones.

15 August 1914: German askari seize Taveta in British East Africa. 'Two companies of Askari (300 men) seized Taveta, on the British side of Mount Kilimanjaro.' Cliopatria draws the 8 Kenya cells from 1915.

26 August 1914: Togoland capitulates. 'The colony surrendered on 26 August 1914 under governor Hans Georg von Doering', after the Kamina wireless station was destroyed on the night of 24/25 August. The land stays German title under Anglo-French occupation (zones from 27 December 1916; mandates 20 July 1922).
26 August 1914: the British zone of Togoland capitulates with the rest of the colony ('The colony surrendered on 26 August 1914'); the British Togoland page dates the occupation 27 August 1914.

26 August 1914: French troops hold the east of Togoland. 'The colony surrendered on 26 August 1914' after 'French and British troops invaded unopposed' on 7 August. Owner side of the occupation that french-africa books in its own ledger (the land stays this state's, hatched in the occupier's colour, until the German title ends on 28 June 1919).

26 August 1914: British troops hold the west of Togoland. The colony surrendered on 26 August 1914 (the British Togoland page dates its occupation to 27 August). Owner side of the occupation that british-togoland books in its own ledger (the land stays this state's, hatched in the occupier's colour, until the German title ends on 28 June 1919).

15 September 1914: the Union of South Africa invades South West Africa. Infobox '15 September 1914 - 9 July 1915'; hostilities opened with the assault on Ramansdrift police station on 13 September 1914 (GSWA page).

region.text: Neukamerun: the part of Cliopatria's 1911 shape that is not in the 1905 shape

ledger.note: 1915: French and Belgian troops occupy Neukamerun. 'In this year most of Neukamerun was occupied by Belgian and French troops'; the page's text places it in late 1915 but states no year. Owner side of the occupation that french-africa books in its own ledger (the land stays this state's, hatched in the occupier's colour, until the German title ends on 28 June 1919).

9 July 1915: South West Africa surrenders. The governor 'surrendered at Korab, north of Windhoek, on 9 July 1915' (the GSWA page: Victor Franke capitulated near Khorab). The colony stays German title under South African occupation until the Treaty of Versailles.

9 July 1915: South West Africa passes to Union forces. 'On 9 July 1915, Victor Franke, the last commander of the Schutztruppe, capitulated near Khorab' after Botha reached Windhuk on 5 May. The occupier is the Union; the british-africa dossier books the same occupation with counterpart german-africa (the Union lies inside Cliopatria's British Africa), so one of the two bookings is a duplicate. Owner side of the occupation that south-africa books in its own ledger (the land stays this state's, hatched in the occupier's colour, until the German title ends on 28 June 1919).

region.text: German East Africa less the Kigoma district

ledger.note: 1916: British and Belgian columns push into German East Africa proper; 'at the Battle of Tabora on 19 September, the Germans were defeated' and 'by September 1916, the German Central Railway ... was fully under British control'. The exact first advance into Tanganyika is not dated on the page.

region.text: Neukamerun: the part of Cliopatria's 1911 shape that is not in the 1905 shape

ledger.note: 1916: the occupation of Neukamerun ends in its return to France. 'During the First World War, in 1916, Neukamerun returned to France' (the french-africa dossier keeps its occupation to 1919 and books the gain then; the page's year is used here).

region.text: Neukamerun: the part of Cliopatria's 1911 shape that is not in the 1905 shape

ledger.note: 1916: Neukamerun returns to France. The Agadir page says that in 1916, during World War I, Neukamerun returned to France. The French dossier records its occupation in 1915 (owner side booked above) and its gain in 1919; the page's year is used here for the end of the occupation and the loss.

March 1916: the British are back at Taveta. The Latema Nek page has the 5th South African Regiment arriving 'in reserve at Taveta, Kenya' on 11 March 1916, the day the attack on Latema Nek began (battle 11-12 March), so the border post was behind British lines by then; no page opened (East African campaign, Salaita Hill of 12 February 1916, Latema Nek) gives the day of the retaking, and Cliopatria's 1916 shape no longer reaches Kenya.

10 March 1916: the Kamerun campaign ends. Infobox '6 August 1914 - 10 March 1916'; 'In February 1916 ... Britain and France agreed to divide Kamerun along the Picot Provisional Partition Line' and the last garrison at Mora surrendered in mid-February.

union.text: Neukamerun: the part of Cliopatria's 1911 shape that is not in the 1905 shape

region.text: the French zone of Kamerun under the Picot line, less Neukamerun, which is booked separately

ledger.note: March 1916: the French zone of Kamerun is held. In February 1916 'Britain and France agreed to divide Kamerun along the Picot Provisional Partition Line' and France received Duala and most of the central plateau; the campaign ends on 10 March 1916 (infobox). Owner side of the occupation that french-africa books in its own ledger (the land stays this state's, hatched in the occupier's colour, until the German title ends on 28 June 1919).

region.text: the British fifth of Kamerun on the Nigerian border

ledger.note: March 1916: the British zone of Kamerun is held. Under the Picot line 'Britain received about one fifth of the colony, on the Nigerian border'; the region (Nord-Ouest and Sud-Ouest) is the researcher's reading of that fifth, and no British Cameroons dossier exists, so british-africa is the counterpart. Owner side of the occupation that british-africa books in its own ledger (the land stays this state's, hatched in the occupier's colour, until the German title ends on 28 June 1919).
18 April 1916: the Belgian Force Publique opens its offensive into Ruanda-Urundi. Kigali was captured on 6 May and 'by 17 June, Burundi and Rwanda were occupied'.

The portuguese-mozambique dossier books only the 1919 gain. Owner side of the occupation that portuguese-mozambique books in its own ledger (the land stays this state's, hatched in the occupier's colour, until the German title ends on 28 June 1919).
17 June 1916: Ruanda-Urundi is occupied. 'by 17 June, Burundi and Rwanda were occupied.' Title stays German until 1919; the Belgian dossier hatches the land from May.

June 1916: Ruanda and Urundi are held by Belgian forces. The Force Publique took Kigali on 6 May and 'by 17 June, Burundi and Rwanda were occupied' (belgian-congo books its occupation from May). Owner side of the occupation that belgian-congo books in its own ledger (the land stays this state's, hatched in the occupier's colour, until the German title ends on 28 June 1919).

'On 23 November, Lettow-Vorbeck crossed into Mozambique'; the Central Railway was 'fully under British control' by September 1916 and Tabora fell on 19 September 1916 (the british-africa dossier books its occupation from 1916 without a month; here it follows the contest). Owner side of the occupation that british-africa books in its own ledger (the land stays this state's, hatched in the occupier's colour, until the German title ends on 28 June 1919).

August 1918: the German column enters Northern Rhodesia. 'crossed into Rhodesia in August 1918'; it reached Kasama on 9 November and made probing attacks there from 12 November.

25 November 1918: Lettow-Vorbeck surrenders. 'at 11:00 a.m. on 25 November 1918, Lettow-Vorbeck offered his surrender to the British at Abercorn (now Mbala)', after word of the armistice on 14 November: the last German force in Africa lays down its arms.

28 June 1919: Germany renounces South West Africa. The colony was not 'officially' ceded 'until the 1919 Treaty of Versailles'; South Africa has administered it as a mandate from 1919 (campaign page). The Union dossier dates its own gain 1920.

28 June 1919: Germany renounces German East Africa. The Supreme Council awarded German East Africa to Britain on 7 May 1919; the Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919 (in force 10 January 1920); the British dossier dates the Tanganyika mandate 20 July 1922.

1919: Ruanda-Urundi passes to Belgium. Britain ceded 'the north-western GEA districts of Ruanda and Urundi to Belgium' under the Anglo-Belgian agreement of 30 May 1919, ratified by the Commission on Mandates on 16 July and accepted by the Supreme Council on 7 August 1919.
1919: the Kionga Triangle returns to Portugal. On 12 July 1919 the Commission on Mandates agreed it 'would be given to Portugal'.

region.text: the British fifth of Kamerun on the Nigerian border

ledger.note: 1919: Kamerun is divided between Britain and France. The partition agreed in February 1916 'was accepted at the Paris Peace Conference' and the colony became mandates by the Treaty of Versailles; Britain got 'approximately one fifth of the colony situated on the Nigerian border'. The provinces named are the researcher's reading of that strip.
1919: French Cameroun. The remainder of Kamerun, about four fifths, becomes a French mandate (Neukamerun already returned to France in 1916).

region.text: British Togoland, the Ghana part of the colony

ledger.note: 1919: Togoland's British zone. Togoland was 'separated into French and British administrative zones' on 27 December 1916 and became Class B mandates on 20 July 1922, the French share 'about two-thirds'. The British share is the Ghana part of Cliopatria's Togoland shape.
1919: Togoland's French zone, the Togo part of the colony (the mandate formally dates from 20 July 1922).

wars.name: Abushiri Revolt
wars.outcome: Put down by the Germans with British help; no territory changed hands.
wars.note: The page: 'The Abushiri Revolt of 1888 was put down with British help the following year.' Nothing more is dated.

wars.name: Herero and Nama genocide
wars.outcome: German reprisals ended both risings; the colony's borders did not change.
wars.note: The page: 'a campaign of reprisals from 1904 to 1908'; the Nama rising was 'finally quashed during 1907-1908'.

wars.name: Maji Maji Rebellion
wars.outcome: Put down by Governor von Götzen; no territory changed hands.
wars.note: The GEA page dates only the start ('Maji Maji Rebellion: 21 October 1905') and the 1907 colonial reform that followed; the end year is not on the page, so 'to' is 1905.

wars.name: Agadir Crisis
wars.outcome: No fighting. The Franco-German Accord of 4 November 1911 recognised French Morocco and gave Germany the 275,000 km2 of Neukamerun.
wars.note: A diplomatic crisis, listed because it moved a border; the territorial change is in the ledger (1911/11), with no contested zone.

wars.name: Togoland campaign
wars.outcome: Allied victory: the colony surrendered on 26 August 1914 after a few skirmishes; British and French zones from 27 December 1916.
wars.note: 'French and British troops invaded unopposed the next day [7 August]'; the Kamina wireless station was destroyed on 24/25 August.

wars.name: Kamerun campaign

zones.text: Neukamerun: the part of Cliopatria's 1911 shape that is not in the 1905 shape

wars.outcome: Allied victory; Kamerun partitioned along the Picot Provisional Partition Line (February 1916), Britain taking about a fifth; mandates 1919.
wars.note: 6 August 1914 to 10 March 1916; Douala fell on 27 September 1914; Germans fled to neutral Spanish Rio Muni.

wars.name: South West Africa campaign
wars.outcome: Allied (South African) victory; the colony capitulated at Khorab on 9 July 1915 and was administered by South Africa as a mandate from 1919.
wars.note: 15 September 1914 to 9 July 1915; the Maritz rebellion of October 1914 to February 1915 helped the Germans briefly.

wars.name: East African campaign (World War I)
wars.outcome: Allied victory: 'German East Africa partitioned by Britain, Belgium and Portugal'. Lettow-Vorbeck's column invaded Mozambique (23 November 1917) and Northern Rhodesia (August 1918) and surrendered at Abercorn on 25 November 1918.
wars.note: 3 August 1914 to 25 November 1918; Tanga (3-5 November 1914) was a German victory; Tabora fell on 19 September 1916.

certainty.note: Protectorates on coastal stretches and company charters; none of the pages opened gives a boundary.

The 1890 Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty 'fixed' South West Africa's boundaries (GSWA page), East Africa's lines were surveyed to 1910 (GEA page) and the 1911 accord fixed Neukamerun; Kamerun's northern and eastern frontiers before 1911 and the Ruanda-Urundi limits are not on the pages and should be treated as soft.
Wartime occupation lines and the Picot Provisional Partition Line (February 1916) of Kamerun; the German column in Mozambique and Rhodesia held no frontier.

notes:
Dossier written by af-08-c from nine pages. Aggregate colonial state (four colonies: Togoland, Kamerun, South West Africa, East Africa); Cliopatria draws them as one row.

Cliopatria problems. (1) The 1871-1884 shape is a 7-cell Douala patch with no support: the pages date German rule from 1884 (the Kamerun dossier of another group has the same patch as 'Kamerun 1868-1870' and names this state as its successor; this dossier starts 1884, so that link is a Cliopatria continuity only). (2) German East Africa is missing from the 1885-1889 shape and all but the coast from 1890-1894, although the GEA page dates the colony from the charter of 27 February 1885; Cliopatria draws the mainland only from 1895. (3) Cliopatria lags the war by a year (Togo kept to 1914, Namibia to 1915) and then drops each colony as it is occupied; this dossier follows the master plan (rule 4: occupied land is hatched in the occupier's colour over the owner's) and keeps the colonies as the German state's land until Versailles (28 June 1919), restoring them in the 1915-1919 keyframes. The 1918 shape is Lettow-Vorbeck's raid on northern Mozambique, recorded as occupation events. (4) Rwanda (1898), Burundi (1900), the Kamerun hinterland (1890, 1895, 1905) and the full extent of South West Africa (1885) are changes in Cliopatria's shapes that none of the nine pages dates; the ledger records them at confidence 1.

Disagreements with other dossiers (for the reviewer): south-africa dates the Namibia gain 1920 and british-africa 1919; british-africa and belgian-congo date the Tanganyika/Ruanda-Urundi mandates 20 July 1922; french-africa dates Neukamerun's return 1919, the Agadir Crisis page says 1916 (used here); french-africa has Togoland's surrender on 27 August 1914, the Togoland page says 26 August; the colonization page puts the Mlapa treaty on 24 April 1884, the Togoland page on 5 July 1884 (used). German title ends here on 28 June 1919 while the occupiers' gains follow in 1920-1922.

Page budget (9 of 9) did not allow: the Togo and Kamerun border treaties (1897-1912), the Hereroland and Maji Maji pages, the Treaty of Versailles page, the Portuguese retaking of Kionga (Portuguese-Mozambique dates it with the 1919 gain), the dates of Rwanda-Urundi's incorporation, Walvis Bay. The Maji Maji war row ends in 1905 only because the page gives no end.

Gazetteer: 'Kionga Triangle' and 'Taveta' are not in the gazetteer; the dossier uses intersects of Cliopatria's own shapes with Mozambique and Kenya instead. No ruler strip (a colonial aggregate has no single ruler; the Kaiser's reigns would be Germany's dossier).


Repairs of 2026-10-25 (review af-08-c; the 9-page budget was exceeded, 22 pages in all, because the repair needed dates the first run did not open). (1) Owner-side occupation events added (the review's blocking finding): Togoland (french-africa, 1914/8), British Togoland (british-togoland, 1914/8), Neukamerun (french-africa, 1915 to 1916), Namibia (south-africa, 1915/7), French Kamerun and the British zone (french-africa and british-africa, 1916/3), Kionga (portuguese-mozambique, 1916/4), Ruanda-Urundi (belgian-congo, 1916/6), Kigoma (belgian-congo, 1916/7) and German East Africa less Kigoma (british-africa, 1917/11), each with an occupation_end on 28 June 1919 and the same counterpart and region. Occupations that overlap in time share counterparts (british-africa: Kamerun zone, Tanganyika, and the German raids on Taveta and Kasama; portuguese-mozambique: Kionga and the German raid), so the compiler must pair start and end by counterpart AND region. Neukamerun: an occupation from 1915 (Kamerun campaign page, year not stated, confidence 2) ends in the 1916 loss the Agadir page gives; french-africa keeps its occupation to 1919 and books the gain then, which this dossier does not mirror. The English page gives no day for the French occupation of Neukamerun, and the same cells (modern Cameroon) are also inside the 1919 loss of 'French Kamerun', which was left as it was. Namibia: south-africa is used as the occupier; british-africa books the same occupation (duplicate). (2) The dissolve region is now the 1919 keyframe (Cliopatria's 1914 shape less Neukamerun). (3) Capitals: Windhuk now starts in 1892 (Otjimbingwe page) with Otjimbingwe from 1885 before it (Goering, GSWA page; 'late 1880s' on the Otjimbingwe page); Togoland has Aného 1885-1887, Zebe 1887-1896 (drawn at Aného) and Lomé from 1897; Kamerun has Douala to 1900 (unverified), Buea 1901-1914 and Jaunde 1914-1916. The Buea page says Buea was capital to 1919 and the campaign page says the Germans were at 'the new capital at Jaunde' in 1915; the two are not reconciled (Buea ended in 1914 here). No page names a capital for 1884. (4) The Sultan's 16 km coastal strip is excluded from the 1885 gain and enters on 28 April 1888 as a lease from people-s-republic-of-zanzibar (Abushiri revolt page), the date the Zanzibar dossier books as its loss; the review proposed 1890, but no page opened mentions an 1890 purchase and the Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty page was not opened. New keyframe 1888-1889. Disagreement kept: a lease is not a cession and German government rule dates from 1 January 1891. (5) Taveta: the 1916 occupation_end is now March 1916 (Latema Nek page: South African troops at Taveta on 11 March) at confidence 2; Kionga: April 1916 (Kionga Triangle page). Thin items tried and not settled: Namibia 1885 (History of Namibia silent), Togoland inland 1890 (Togoland Neutral Zone page failed to load; German Togoland page: no date), Kamerun hinterland (Adamawa page: southern Adamawa invaded January 1898, Tibati by 1901, nothing on 1893-1894 or on 1890, 1895 and 1905), Rwanda (Ruanda-Urundi page: German presence by alliance 1897, a year before Cliopatria) and Burundi (Treaty of Kiganda page failed to load). Failed pages: Treaty_of_Kiganda, Togoland_Neutral_Zone, Zébé.
